page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1572.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the lower tiers. The multi-core stress-ng score is 4147.67, and uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 28.26 GB/sec. The instance supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and neural network inference, as demonstrated by an average text generation speed of 74.92 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute resources without the performance variability of shared-core instances, though the overall resource density is modest. Given the average single-threaded performance and lower multi-core scaling, this instance is suited for workloads that benefit from high clock speeds but do not require massive parallelization or high memory bandwidth. Appropriate workloads include light web serving, single-threaded batch processing, and basic text processing tasks.
